title: Fish vertebral processes are set at about 120° to one another for uniform stiffness

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Fish vertebral processes are set at about 120° to one another for uniform stiffness

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In ordinary fishes such as cod and haddock (and partly in whales), the backbone is stiffened by three series of ligament-connected processes, dorsal and two transverse, arranged at nearly equal angles of 120°, which gives the greatest and most uniform strength possible for such a system.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: three series of processes at \approx 120^\circ to one another

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVI: On Form and Mechanical Efficiency

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And here we see (as we see partly also among the whales), that these three series of processes, or struts, tend to be arranged well-nigh at equal angles, of 120°, with one another, giving the greatest and most uniform strength of which such a system is capable.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVI, “On Form and Mechanical Efficiency”; topic “Aquatic animals and stiffness”. Scope: vertebral columns of round-bodied fishes and cetaceans

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: three series of processes at \approx 120^\circ to one another

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch16-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The 120-degree prediction and mechanical optimum are quantitative. Public morphology can test the geometry broadly, but the claim about greatest uniform strength requires material and ligament properties rarely paired with scans.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure angular separation of dorsal and transverse vertebral processes in 3D fish and cetacean scans, then use beam models to compare stiffness isotropy at observed versus alternative angles.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Ligaments and soft tissues needed for stiffness are usually absent.

Processes vary along the column.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The 120-degree arrangement is a direct angular measurement on existing vertebral CT. Coverage is good enough for a sample of fishes and some whales and is not yet a survey of round-bodied fishes. The stiffness-maximizing interpretation can be checked with a simple structural model once the angles are in hand, so the geometric half of the claim is the part current scans can settle.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On vertebrae of round-bodied fishes such as cod and haddock, and on whale vertebrae, measure the angles among the neural spine and the two transverse processes. The geometric claim is supported if those angles cluster near 120 degrees; a strong departure toward a different symmetric or asymmetric arrangement would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Angles are not pre-tabulated and must be measured from scans that are uneven across ordinary round-bodied fishes.

The further claim that 120 degrees maximizes uniform stiffness needs a separate mechanical model of the ligament system.
